The CUA and POE hearings are the critical path and can run in parallel; the building permit and health permit follow sequentially. The day range sums the minimum and maximum times for approvals that can overlap (CUA and POE in parallel) and then adds the building and health permits in sequence; actual elapsed time will be 8–18 months if the CUA and POE are filed together and no appeals are taken. The cost range sums the four catalog entries' fees and does not include the ABC Type 42 license acquisition cost, which is unknown because the applicant must either apply for a new original license ($1,000–$1,600 per catalog:ca.abc_type_42, plus PCN processing if the tract is over-concentrated) or purchase and transfer a Type 42 from another bar within the Mission SUD (market price unknown, likely $5,000–$50,000 for a beer-wine license in San Francisco, versus $100,000+ for a Type 47 full-liquor license). The cost also excludes architect and consultant fees, construction costs, the business registration ($55–$700 per catalog:sf.business_registration), entity formation ($70–$150 per catalog:ca.sos_entity_registration), fictitious business name ($60–$120 per catalog:sf.fictitious_business_name), workers' comp insurance (percentage of payroll per catalog:ca.workers_comp_insurance), and other state and federal registrations. outcomes.original: Estimated time: 210 to 545 days. Estimated government cost: $8,426 to $23,650. Notes: These figures are the time to approval and government cost for the four approvals in the entitlement path when they are granted: Conditional Use Authorization (120–300 days, $3,100–$15,000 per catalog:sf.conditional_use_authorization), Place of Entertainment permit (45–120 days, $2,708–$3,800 per catalog:sf.place_of_entertainment_permit), health permit to operate (14–45 days for plan check plus permit, $828–$2,500 plan check and $470–$1,000 permit per catalog:sf.health_plan_check and catalog:sf.health_permit), and building permit with change of use (14–120 days, $800–$15,000 per catalog:sf.building_permit). The CUA and POE hearings are the critical path and can run in parallel; the building permit and health permit follow sequentially. The day range sums the minimum and maximum times for approvals that can overlap (CUA and POE in parallel) and then adds the building and health permits in sequence; actual elapsed time will be 8–18 months if the CUA and POE are filed together and no appeals are taken. The cost range sums the four catalog entries' fees and does not include the ABC Type 42 license acquisition cost, which is unknown because the applicant must either apply for a new original license ($1,000–$1,600 per catalog:ca.abc_type_42, plus PCN processing if the tract is over-concentrated) or purchase and transfer a Type 42 from another bar within the Mission SUD (market price unknown, likely $5,000–$50,000 for a beer-wine license in San Francisco, versus $100,000+ for a Type 47 full-liquor license). The cost also excludes architect and consultant fees, construction costs, the business registration ($55–$700 per catalog:sf.business_registration), entity formation ($70–$150 per catalog:ca.sos_entity_registration), fictitious business name ($60–$120 per catalog:sf.fictitious_business_name), workers' comp insurance (percentage of payroll per catalog:ca.workers_comp_insurance), and other state and federal registrations. If the CUA or POE application is denied or appealed, no time or cost to approval is given because the figures above are for granted approvals only.
